page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture using AWS Neoverse-V2 cores, this server features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and features a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory subsystem performance. The c8gn.16xlarge achieves top-tier results in memory bandwidth, reaching 7395.26 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 466.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Multi-threaded operations perform exceptionally well, as evidenced by top-tier scores in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, Geekbench multi-core testing, and Passmark database operations. Redis SET operations reach 144.9 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 116.84 GB/sec. However, single-core performance remains average, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the middle 50% of tested servers.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the c8gn.16xlarge is driven by its high physical core density and ARM-based architecture, which typically offers favorable performance-per-watt compared to traditional x86 architectures. Tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage, requiring reliance on network-attached EBS volumes, and the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive datasets. Additionally, while text generation on medium and large LLM models is relatively strong, text generation on small models is weak. This instance is best suited for compute-heavy, highly parallelized workloads such as software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, static web serving, and network-bound applications.

It features 128.0 GB of memory, 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor without local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core and memory bandwidth performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 466.64 GB/sec and static web serving throughput at 116.84 GB/sec.
